title: Compact Laplace Type Operators And Hodge Representatives

items.title: Second-order Laplace-type operators on metric vector bundles
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary of
dimension $n\ge2$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]), let $\mu$ be a smooth positive
density on $M$ ([[def-density-bundle-and-smooth-density]]), and let $E\to M$ be
a finite-rank smooth vector bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-bundle-rank-fibre-and-trivial-bundle]]) over
$\mathbb K=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ carrying a smooth bundle metric
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ ([[def-smooth-bundle-metric]]), Euclidean in the
real case and Hermitian, linear in the first variable, in the complex case; in
the complex case the fibres are complex vector spaces through a smooth complex
structure on $E$
([[def-complex-linear-and-compatible-bundle-connections]]). Write $\Gamma(E)$
for the smooth sections ([[def-smooth-section-local-section-and-support]]).

A $\mathbb K$-linear map $P:\Gamma(E)\to\Gamma(E)$ is a **linear differential
operator of order at most two** on $E$ when, on every chart domain $\Omega$ of
$M$ with coordinates $x=(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$ and in every local frame of $E$ over
$\Omega$ in which a section is written $s\leftrightarrow u=(u^1,\ldots,u^r)$
and its image as $Ps\leftrightarrow((Ps)_1,\ldots,(Ps)_r)$,
$$(Ps)_\lambda=-\sum_{i,j=1}^na^{ij}_{\lambda\mu}(x)\,\partial_i\partial_ju^\mu(x)+\sum_{j=1}^nb^j_{\lambda\mu}(x)\,\partial_ju^\mu(x)+c_{\lambda\mu}(x)u^\mu(x),\qquad1\le\lambda\le r,$$
with smooth coefficient functions on $\Omega$ and summation over the repeated
index $\mu$ (and over $i,j$). Such an operator is **Laplace type** when in
addition, in every such chart and frame, its second-order coefficients are
scalar multiples of the identity, $a^{ij}_{\lambda\mu}=a^{ij}\delta_{\lambda\mu}$,
with $a^{ij}$ smooth real functions for which the matrix $(a^{ij}(x))$ is
symmetric and positive definite at every $x\in\Omega$. Its **principal symbol**
is the endomorphism-valued quadratic function
$\sigma_2(P)(x,\xi)=a^{ij}(x)\xi_i\xi_j\,\mathrm{id}_{E_x}$ for
$\xi\in T_x^*M$. Its scalar principal form $a$ is a smooth section of
$\mathrm{Sym}^2TM$ ([[def-smooth-tensor-field]]), since it acts on two
covectors, and $a_x(\xi,\xi)>0$ for $\xi\ne0$. For positive-rank $E$ the
symbol determines $a$ uniquely. On the zero-rank bundle the operator and its
symbol are zero; a supplied smooth positive-definite form $a$ is part of the
Laplace-type data in this degenerate case.

For the density-integral convention assume Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]). $P$ is **formally symmetric** for
$(\mu,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ when
$$\int_M\langle Ps,t\rangle\,d\mu=\int_M\langle s,Pt\rangle\,d\mu$$
for all compactly supported smooth sections $s,t\in\Gamma_c(E)$
([[def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-smooth-density]]).

**Well-definedness.** The definition is local. On a fixed chart and frame the
displayed assignment is a $\mathbb K$-linear map on components with smooth
coefficients, and the chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]])
computes the transition to another chart and frame on the overlap: the
second-order coefficients transform by the symmetric tensor rule
$a'^{kl}=a^{ij}\frac{\partial x'^k}{\partial x^i}\frac{\partial x'^l}{\partial x^j}$
together with conjugation by the frame-change matrix, while the terms produced
by the second derivatives of the coordinate change are absorbed into the
first-order coefficients. Hence a single operator that admits a local
expression on one cover admits a local expression on every chart and frame, and
the two hypotheses placed on the leading coefficient are invariant: scalar-ness
is preserved by frame conjugation and by the coordinate rule for a field of
symmetric matrices, and symmetric positive definiteness is preserved by both.
For positive rank the scalar principal form, and in every rank the principal
symbol, are therefore independent of the chart and frame, since two
local expressions of the same operator differ by an operator of order at most
one; the symbol is smooth in $(x,\xi)$ because the $a^{ij}$ are smooth, and
the scalar principal form is positive on nonzero covectors exactly when
$(a^{ij})$ is positive definite.
Formal symmetry is an identity between integrals of compactly supported smooth
sections and therefore depends only on the operator, the density and the
metric.
items.strategy: The definition is local. On a fixed chart and frame the displayed assignment is a $\mathbb K$-linear map on components with smooth coefficients, and the chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) computes the transition to another chart and frame on the overlap: the second-order coefficients transform by the symmetric tensor rule $a'^{kl}=a^{ij}\frac{\partial x'^k}{\partial x^i}\frac{\partial x'^l}{\partial x^j}$ and by conjugation with the frame-change matrix, while the terms produced by the second derivatives of the coordinate change are absorbed into the first-order coefficients. Hence a single operator that admits a local expression on one cover admits a local expression on every chart and frame, and the two hypotheses placed on the leading coefficient are invariant: scalar-ness is preserved by frame conjugation and by the coordinate rule for a field of symmetric matrices, and symmetric positive definiteness is preserved by both. The principal symbol is therefore independent of the chart and frame (the order-two part is well defined because two local expressions of the same operator differ by an operator of order at most one), it is smooth in $(x,\xi)$ because the $a^{ij}$ are smooth, and it is positive on nonzero covectors exactly when $(a^{ij})$ is positive definite. Formal symmetry is an identity between integrals of compactly supported smooth sections and therefore depends only on the operator, the density and the metric. No choice is used and no existence of densities, metrics or partitions is asserted.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice inherited solely by the density-integral definition of formal symmetry; local symbol calculations use supplied data and no choice.

items.title: Formal adjoints of differential operators on metric vector bundles
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the density-integral
convention. Let $M$ be a Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary,
$\mu$ a smooth positive density on $M$, and $E,F\to M$ finite-rank smooth vector
bundles over $\mathbb K=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ with smooth bundle metrics,
Hermitian (first-variable-linear) in the complex case, with the conventions of
[[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]]. Let
$P:\Gamma(E)\to\Gamma(F)$ be a linear differential operator of order at most two
(the target-$F$ version of the local description in
[[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]]).

Then there is a unique linear differential operator $P^\star:\Gamma(F)\to\Gamma(E)$
of order at most two such that
$$\int_M\langle Pu,v\rangle_F\,d\mu=\int_M\langle u,P^\star v\rangle_E\,d\mu$$
for all compactly supported smooth sections $u\in\Gamma_c(E)$ and
$v\in\Gamma_c(F)$; it is the **formal adjoint** of $P$. It is given locally as
follows: in a chart with coordinates $x$, with density coefficient $\gamma>0$
defined by $\mu=\gamma\,|dx^1\cdots dx^n|$
([[def-density-bundle-and-smooth-density]]), with frames of $E$ and $F$
orthonormal for the metrics (equivalently unitary in the complex case; such
frames exist locally by applying Gram–Schmidt to any local frame,
[[thm-gram-schmidt-orthonormalisation]]), and with local coefficients
$Pu=\sum_{|\alpha|\le2}a_\alpha D^\alpha u$,
$$P^\star v=\sum_{|\alpha|\le2}(-1)^{|\alpha|}\gamma^{-1}D^\alpha\bigl(\gamma\,a_\alpha^*v\bigr),$$
where $a_\alpha^*$ is the fibre adjoint. Consequently:
1. if the leading coefficients of $P$ of order $\delta\in\{0,1,2\}$ are the
   matrices $a_\alpha$, $|\alpha|=\delta$, then those of $P^\star$ are
   $(-1)^\delta a_\alpha^*$, computed in the same orthonormal frames; in
   particular the formal adjoint of a Laplace-type operator is again Laplace
   type and its principal symbol is unchanged,
   $\sigma_2(P^\star)=\sigma_2(P)$;
2. $(P^\star)^\star=P$;
3. if $E=F$, then $P$ is formally symmetric in the sense of
   [[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]] exactly when
   $P=P^\star$.
items.strategy: Local construction. In a chart with orthonormal frames and density coefficient $\gamma$, integrate the product $(Pu)_\lambda\overline{v}_\lambda\gamma$ by parts $|\alpha|$ times; each step cancels the boundary term because $u$ and $v$ have compact support ([[lem-euclidean-stokes-for-a-compactly-supported-form]] applied to the compactly supported $(n-1)$-forms built from the products), and the derivatives falling on $\gamma$ and on $a_\alpha$ produce exactly the displayed formula. Uniqueness on an open set: if a smooth operator $Q$ satisfies $\int\langle Pu,v\rangle=\int\langle u,Qv\rangle$ for all compactly supported smooth $u,v$ in a chart, then for fixed $v$ the section $Qv$ vanishes wherever it is nonzero-free: if a component of $Qv$ were nonzero at a point, a compactly supported $u$ equal to a nonnegative cutoff times that component near the point would make the integral nonzero, a contradiction. Gluing: over an overlap of two charts, the two locally constructed operators both satisfy the adjoint identity against tests supported in the overlap, so their difference $R$ satisfies $\int\langle u,Rv\rangle=0$ for all such tests and hence vanishes there by the previous paragraph; the local operators therefore agree on overlaps and patch to one global smooth operator $P^\star$, which is unique by the same argument. The local formula shows that $P^\star$ has order at most that of $P$ and gives the symbol identity in (1), since the top-order part of $\gamma^{-1}D^\alpha(\gamma a_\alpha^*v)$ is $(-1)^{|\alpha|}a_\alpha^*D^\alpha v$. Applying the defining identity twice and using uniqueness gives $(P^\star)^\star=P$, and (3) is the defining identity itself. The construction is made over the given atlas and uses no choice, no partition of unity and no global pseudodifferential calculus.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice inherited by density integration; all chart localization and frame selections in the proof are finite or local.

items.title: Complex manifolds, holomorphic vector bundles and Hermitian metrics
items.statement:
Let $m\ge1$. A **chart** on a topological space $X$ is a homeomorphism
$\varphi:U\to\varphi(U)$ from an open set $U\subseteq X$ onto an open subset of
$\mathbb C^m$ with its usual topology ([[def-homeomorphism-and-open-maps]]);
two charts $\varphi,\psi$ are **holomorphically compatible** when the
transition maps $\psi\circ\varphi^{-1}$ and $\varphi\circ\psi^{-1}$ are
holomorphic on the open sets where they are defined
([[def-holomorphic-function-in-several-complex-variables]]). A **holomorphic
atlas** is a family of pairwise compatible charts whose domains cover $X$. A
**complex manifold of dimension $m$** is a nonempty Hausdorff
([[def-hausdorff-space]]) second-countable ([[def-second-countable-space]])
topological space carrying a holomorphic atlas; the same maximal-atlas argument
as for [[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]] applies verbatim with
$\mathbb C^m$ in place of $\mathbb C$: the union of a holomorphic atlas with all
charts compatible with it is again a holomorphic atlas, so one passes to the
unique maximal atlas and calls its members holomorphic charts. Each chart is a
homeomorphism onto an open subset of $\mathbb C^m\cong\mathbb R^{2m}$, so $X$ is
a topological manifold without boundary of real dimension $2m$
([[def-topological-manifold-without-boundary]]), and for connected $X$ the case
$m=1$ recovers Riemann surfaces ([[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]]).

A **holomorphic map** $f:X\to Y$ between complex manifolds is a continuous map
whose expression in every pair of holomorphic charts is holomorphic
([[def-holomorphic-map-and-complex-jacobian]]); equivalently, for every open
$V\subseteq Y$ and every holomorphic function $h$ on $V$, the function
$h\circ f$ is holomorphic on $f^{-1}(V)$. The forward implication is the
holomorphic chain rule; conversely apply this condition to the coordinate
functions of a chart on $Y$.

**Induced smooth structure and complex structure.** Holomorphic functions on
open subsets of $\mathbb C^m$ are smooth
([[cor-holomorphic-functions-in-several-variables-are-smooth]]), so every
holomorphic atlas is a smooth atlas ([[def-smooth-atlas]]) and $X$ is a smooth
manifold of real dimension $2m$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]) whose smooth charts
include the holomorphic ones. In holomorphic coordinates
$z_k=x_k+iy_k$ the **complex structure** is the endomorphism field $J$ of the
tangent bundle determined by $J\partial_{x_k}=\partial_{y_k}$ and
$J\partial_{y_k}=-\partial_{x_k}$; it satisfies $J^2=-\mathrm{id}$ and is
independent of the holomorphic chart, because a holomorphic transition map has
complex-linear differential ([[def-holomorphic-map-and-complex-jacobian]],
[[thm-chain-rule-for-holomorphic-maps-in-several-variables]]) and complex-linear
maps intertwine the two coordinate definitions of multiplication by $i$. A
**Hermitian metric** on $X$ is a Riemannian metric $g$
([[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]]) satisfying
$g(Jv,Jw)=g(v,w)$ for all tangent vectors $v,w$; its Riemannian volume density
is written $\mu_g$ ([[def-riemannian-volume-density]]). The complex structure
makes each tangent space a complex vector space, so the tangent bundle is a
smooth complex vector bundle in the sense of
[[def-complex-linear-and-compatible-bundle-connections]].

**Holomorphic vector bundles and Hermitian bundle metrics.** A **holomorphic
vector bundle of rank $r$** on $X$ is a smooth complex vector bundle
$\pi:E\to X$ of rank $r$
([[def-smooth-vector-bundle-rank-fibre-and-trivial-bundle]],
[[def-complex-linear-and-compatible-bundle-connections]]) together with an open
cover $(V_\alpha)$ of $X$ and smooth local trivializations
$\theta_\alpha:E|_{V_\alpha}\to V_\alpha\times\mathbb C^r$ whose transition
matrices $g_{\alpha\beta}:V_\alpha\cap V_\beta\to\mathrm{GL}_r(\mathbb C)$,
defined by $\theta_\alpha\theta_\beta^{-1}(p,v)=(p,g_{\alpha\beta}(p)v)$, are
holomorphic. A **holomorphic frame** over an open set $V$ is a smooth
complex-linear trivialization whose transition matrices with the supplied
trivializations are holomorphic on every overlap. Changing holomorphic frame multiplies a local section by a
holomorphic matrix, hence a smooth local section is **holomorphic** exactly when
its representatives in holomorphic frames are holomorphic functions. A
**Hermitian metric** $h$ on $E$ is a smooth bundle metric
([[def-smooth-bundle-metric]]) whose fibre pairings are positive definite
Hermitian forms, linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the
second; the condition is frame-independent because the gauge freedom is
conjugation by a pointwise invertible matrix. Smooth sections are
$\Gamma(E)$ ([[def-smooth-section-local-section-and-support]]).
items.strategy: Maximal atlas: the argument of [[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]] applies verbatim with $\mathbb C^m$ in place of $\mathbb C$; pairwise compatibility of a family of charts means all transition maps are holomorphic, and the union of a holomorphic atlas with all charts compatible with it is again a holomorphic atlas, giving the unique maximal atlas. Holomorphic functions of several variables are of class $C^\infty$ ([[cor-holomorphic-functions-in-several-variables-are-smooth]]), so each transition map is a smooth diffeomorphism between open subsets of $\mathbb R^{2m}$ and the maximal holomorphic atlas is a smooth atlas; the induced smooth structure is the one used for tangent vectors, densities and smooth sections ([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Complex structure: on the overlap of two holomorphic charts the transition differential is complex-linear ([[thm-chain-rule-for-holomorphic-maps-in-several-variables]] and the complex Jacobian of [[def-holomorphic-map-and-complex-jacobian]]), so it intertwines the two local definitions of $J$, which is therefore a globally defined smooth endomorphism field with $J^2=-\mathrm{id}$; the tangent bundle is thereby a smooth complex vector bundle in the sense of [[def-complex-linear-and-compatible-bundle-connections]]. Holomorphic bundle: the transition matrices of a holomorphic bundle are holomorphic functions with values in $\mathrm{GL}_r(\mathbb C)$; conversely the given data produce a smooth complex vector bundle by [[def-smooth-vector-bundle-rank-fibre-and-trivial-bundle]] and the cocycle identities, and changing holomorphic frame multiplies a local section by a holomorphic matrix. Hermitian bundle metric: the fibrewise positive definite Hermitian forms vary smoothly in the sense of [[def-smooth-bundle-metric]], and the condition is independent of the chosen trivializations because the only gauge freedom is conjugation by a pointwise invertible matrix. All statements are local verifications; no choice is used and no existence of metrics is asserted.
items.axiom_use: None: the structures are supplied data; the maximal-atlas and gluing verifications are local and choice-free. Existence of compatible or Hermitian metrics is not asserted here.

items.title: E-valued Dolbeault operators and their L2 structure
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for density integration and
completion. Let $X$ be a complex manifold of dimension $m\ge1$
([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]) with a Hermitian
metric $g$, and let $E\to X$ be a holomorphic vector bundle of rank $r$ with a
Hermitian metric $h$ ([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]).
Fix integers $p,q\ge0$. In a holomorphic chart with coordinates
$z=(z_1,\ldots,z_m)$ and a holomorphic frame of $E$, an **$E$-valued
$(p,q)$-form** is an expression
$$s=\sum_{|I|=p}\sum_{|J|=q}s_{IJ}\otimes dz^I\wedge d\bar z^J,$$
with $s_{IJ}$ smooth local sections of $E$ and increasing multi-indices $I,J$
([[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]]); such expressions agree on
overlaps because holomorphic changes of coordinates preserve bidegree and
holomorphic frame changes are complex-linear. The resulting smooth global
sections of the bundle $\Lambda^{p,q}T^*X\otimes E$ are denoted
$\mathcal A^{p,q}(X,E)$; the bundle is zero, and so is
$\mathcal A^{p,q}(X,E)$, when $p>m$ or $q>m$.

The **Dolbeault operator** is the first-order operator
$$\bar\partial_E:\mathcal A^{p,q}(X,E)\to\mathcal A^{p,q+1}(X,E),\qquad \bar\partial_E s=\sum_{I,J}\sum_{k=1}^m \bar\partial_{z_k}s_{IJ}\otimes d\bar z_k\wedge dz^I\wedge d\bar z^J,$$
with the Wirtinger operators $\bar\partial_{z_k}$
([[def-wirtinger-operators-in-several-complex-variables]],
[[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]]) acting componentwise on the local
sections $s_{IJ}$. It is independent of the holomorphic chart and frame, and
$\bar\partial_E^2=0$
([[thm-d-dbar-decomposition-and-identities]]); both assertions are proved
below.

Equip $\Lambda^{p,q}T^*X\otimes E$ with the Hermitian metric induced by $g$ and
$h$ ([[prop-riemannian-metrics-induce-metrics-on-dual-tensor-and-exterior-bundles]]
and [[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]). For compactly
supported smooth $s,t\in\mathcal A^{p,q}(X,E)$ the **$L^2$ pairing**
$$\langle s,t\rangle_{L^2}=\int_X\langle s,t\rangle\,d\mu_g$$
uses the Riemannian volume density $\mu_g$
([[def-riemannian-volume-density]],
[[def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-smooth-density]]) and is a complex
inner product in the first-variable-linear convention
([[def-complex-l-two-inner-product]]); its completion
$L^2(X,\Lambda^{p,q}T^*X\otimes E)$ is a complex Hilbert space
by the completion argument below, using
[[thm-metric-completion-carries-a-unique-banach-space-structure]]. By
[[lem-formal-adjoints-of-differential-operators-exist-and-are-unique]] the
operator $\bar\partial_E$ has a **formal adjoint**
$\bar\partial_E^*:\mathcal A^{p,q+1}(X,E)\to\mathcal A^{p,q}(X,E)$, the unique
smooth first-order operator with
$$\langle\bar\partial_Es,t\rangle_{L^2}=\langle s,\bar\partial_E^*t\rangle_{L^2}$$
for all compactly supported smooth forms.

The **Dolbeault Laplacian**
$\Delta_{\bar\partial_E}=\bar\partial_E\bar\partial_E^*+\bar\partial_E^*\bar\partial_E$
is a formally symmetric Laplace-type second-order operator
([[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]]) preserving each
bidegree $(p,q)$, with
$$\langle\Delta_{\bar\partial_E}s,s\rangle_{L^2}=\|\bar\partial_Es\|_2^2+\|\bar\partial_E^*s\|_2^2\ge0$$
for compactly supported smooth $s$. Its principal symbol is
$\sigma_2(\Delta_{\bar\partial_E})(x,\xi)=|\xi^{0,1}|_g^2\,\mathrm{id}$, where
$\xi^{0,1}$ is the $(0,1)$-part of $\xi\in T_x^*X$; in particular the principal
form is smooth, and it is positive definite on nonzero real covectors.
items.strategy: Well-definedness of $\bar\partial_E$: if $\theta_\alpha,\theta_\beta$ are holomorphic frames with transition matrix $g_{\alpha\beta}$, then $\bar\partial(g_{\alpha\beta}s^\beta)=\bar\partial g_{\alpha\beta}\wedge s^\beta+g_{\alpha\beta}\bar\partial s^\beta=g_{\alpha\beta}\bar\partial s^\beta$, because $g_{\alpha\beta}$ is holomorphic; hence the local $(p,q+1)$-forms glue to a global form. A holomorphic change of coordinates has complex-linear Jacobian ([[def-holomorphic-map-and-complex-jacobian]]) and preserves the bidegree decomposition and commutes with $\bar\partial$ ([[thm-d-dbar-decomposition-and-identities]], [[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]]), so the definition does not depend on the chart. The square vanishes by the coordinate identity $\bar\partial^2=0$ of [[thm-d-dbar-decomposition-and-identities]] plus the same gluing argument. Formal adjoint: $\bar\partial_E$ is a smooth first-order operator between metric bundles over the manifold $X$ with the positive density $\mu_g$, so [[lem-formal-adjoints-of-differential-operators-exist-and-are-unique]] applies and supplies existence, uniqueness and the local formula for $\bar\partial_E^*$. Formal symmetry of the Laplacian: for compactly supported smooth $s,t$, $\langle\bar\partial_E\bar\partial_E^*s,t\rangle+\langle\bar\partial_E^*\bar\partial_Es,t\rangle=\langle\bar\partial_E^*s,\bar\partial_E^*t\rangle+\langle\bar\partial_Es,\bar\partial_Et\rangle$, and each summand is conjugate-symmetric in $s,t$, giving $\langle\Delta_{\bar\partial_E}s,t\rangle=\langle s,\Delta_{\bar\partial_E}t\rangle$; the energy identity is the same expansion with $s=t$. Principal symbol: in a holomorphic chart the operator $D=\bar\partial$ is, on the $(p,q)$-bundle, exterior multiplication by the $(0,1)$-form $\bar\partial z_k\otimes\cdot$ followed by coefficient differentiation, with principal symbol $i\varepsilon(\xi^{0,1})$ in the convention of [[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]] and [[thm-d-dbar-decomposition-and-identities]]; its adjoint has symbol $-i\varepsilon(\xi^{0,1})^*$. The elementary identity $\varepsilon(\eta)\varepsilon(\eta)^*+\varepsilon(\eta)^*\varepsilon(\eta)=|\eta|^2\mathrm{id}$, checked on wedge monomials by deleting each factor with its alternating sign, gives $\sigma_2(DD^*+D^*D)(x,\xi)=|\xi^{0,1}|^2\mathrm{id}$, which is smooth in $(x,\xi)$; for a nonzero real covector the $(0,1)$-part is nonzero, so the form is positive definite. Bidegree preservation and nonnegativity follow because $\bar\partial_E$ raises $q$ by one and $\bar\partial_E^*$ lowers it by one. The metric on $\Lambda^{p,q}T^*X$ is the complex-linear extension of the metric induced on exterior bundles by the compatible Riemannian metric $g$ ([[prop-riemannian-metrics-induce-metrics-on-dual-tensor-and-exterior-bundles]]); the completion statement is ordinary $L^2$ completeness of a metric bundle over a Riemannian manifold with the density measure, obtained from the cited scalar Hilbert-space items on a finite trivializing cover.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice inherited from density integration and Banach completion; the extended integral inner product is constructed by Cauchy pairing limits in Proof 1.2. Local Dolbeault gluing, square-zero and symbol algebra use supplied data only.

items.title: Compact Laplace-type bundle operators: regularity and shifted parametrices
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold without boundary of real dimension $n\ge2$, equipped with a smooth positive density, and $E\to M$ a finite-rank real Euclidean or complex Hermitian smooth vector bundle. Let $P$ be a Laplace-type second-order differential operator on $E$ in the sense of [[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]] — smooth coefficients, formally symmetric for the density and metric, whose positive-frequency principal symbol is
$$\sigma_2(P)(x,\xi)=a_x(\xi,\xi)\,\mathrm{id}_{E_x},$$
where $a$ is a smooth positive-definite real quadratic form on cotangent vectors; thus in any local frame $P=-a^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j+B^j\partial_j+C$, with scalar real positive-definite $a^{ij}$ and matrix-valued lower coefficients. Nonnegativity of $P$ is not needed here.

For nonnegative integers $k$, define $H^k(M,E)$ by requiring the coefficients of each member of a finite smooth partition of unity times the section, in precompact bundle charts and extended by zero, to lie in $H^k(\mathbb R^n)$ ([[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]], [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]); the norm is the square root of the sum of these component Sobolev norms squared. Different such choices give equivalent norms. The following hold.

1. These are Hilbert spaces, smooth sections are dense, $H^0=L^2$ with equivalent norms, $H^{k+1}\hookrightarrow H^k$ is compact, and $H^k\hookrightarrow C^r$ continuously whenever $k>r+n/2$.
2. If $u\in H^1$ and $Pu=f\in H^k$ distributionally, then $u\in H^{k+2}$ and
$$\|u\|_{H^{k+2}}\le C_k(\|f\|_{H^k}+\|u\|_{L^2}).$$
In particular smooth data give smooth weak solutions. The same estimate holds for all $u\in H^{k+2}$.
3. For sufficiently large real $\lambda>0$, $P+\lambda:H^2\to L^2$ is a bounded bijection with bounded inverse $B:L^2\to H^2$. As an operator on $L^2$, $B$ is compact, injective and selfadjoint, has dense range $H^2$, and the unbounded operator $P$ with domain exactly $H^2$ is selfadjoint. The map $B:H^k\to H^{k+2}$ is bounded for every nonnegative integer $k$ and preserves smooth sections.
4. It supplies two-sided parametrices **modulo compact operators**:
$$PB=I-\lambda B\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad BP=I-\lambda B\quad\hbox{on }H^2.$$
Here on the second space $B$ denotes its restriction after inclusion $H^2\hookrightarrow L^2$; it is compact on $H^2$. No assertion concerning arbitrary-order elliptic operators, or pseudodifferential symbol classes, is part of this theorem.
items.strategy:
Chart norms (1): choose finitely many relatively compact bundle charts and a subordinate smooth partition of unity ([[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]], under AC). Coefficient transformation between charts is multiplication by a smooth invertible matrix followed by a smooth coordinate change with bounded derivatives and inverse derivatives on the compact overlaps; the repeated chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) expresses each derivative of order at most $k$ of a transformed coefficient as a finite sum of bounded coefficients times derivatives of order at most $k$ of the original, and integrable change of variables ([[cor-c-one-change-of-variables-for-l-one-functions]]) bounds the integrals; approximate compactly supported Sobolev coefficients by smooth ones ([[cor-compactly-supported-smooth-functions-are-dense-in-wkp-of-rn]]) and pass the bounds to the limit. This gives equivalent norms on different choices and $H^0=L^2$; completeness is checked componentwise, and smooth density follows by localizing, mollifying and summing. Compactness of $H^{k+1}\hookrightarrow H^k$ and the $C^r$ bound follow by applying Rellich compactness and the higher-order Sobolev embedding on finitely many fixed Euclidean balls to the finitely many localized coefficients ([[thm-rellich-compactness-from-w-one-p-to-lp-on-an-extension-domain]], [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]]); the Hilbert-space facts are [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]] and [[lem-w-one-two-is-a-hilbert-space]].

Weak $H^1$-to-$H^2$ regularity (2, $k=0$): in a precompact chart write each component of $Pu=f$ as $-\partial_i(a^{ij}\partial_ju_\alpha)=f_\alpha-\widetilde B^j_{\alpha\beta}\partial_ju_\beta-C_{\alpha\beta}u_\beta$, where the adjusted first-order coefficients absorb the derivatives of $a$; for $u\in H^1$ the right side is locally $L^2$ and bounded by $C(\|f\|_2+\|u\|_{H^1})$ on an outer patch, so the weak scalar interior $H^2$ regularity theorem ([[thm-interior-h-two-regularity-for-divergence-form-equations]]) gives all components in $H^2$ on an inner patch. Cover $M$ by finitely many inner patches inside larger outer patches to get $\|u\|_{H^2}\le C(\|f\|_{L^2}+\|u\|_{H^1})$. Interpolation ([[lem-interpolation-absorbs-lower-order-sobolev-terms-in-elliptic-estimates]]) gives $\|u\|_{H^1}\le\varepsilon\|u\|_{H^2}+C_\varepsilon\|u\|_2$; absorbing the small term yields the stated $k=0$ estimate. Higher order: differentiate the scalar principal equation $k$ times on nested patches; for every multi-index $\alpha$ of length $k$, $w=\partial^\alpha u_\beta\in H^1$ satisfies the same scalar equation with source $\partial^\alpha f_\beta$ plus terms involving at most $k+1$ derivatives of $u$ (the commutator with the principal term always has at least one derivative on $a$), all $L^2$ and bounded by $C_k(\|f\|_{H^k}+\|u\|_{H^{k+1}})$; apply the scalar theorem on successively smaller patches, sum, and absorb the $H^{k+1}$ norm by interpolation again. Smooth data therefore give smooth weak solutions.

Coercivity and the shifted inverse (3): the form $a(u,v)$ obtained from $(Pu,v)_{L^2}$ by integrating the principal term once is bounded on $H^1\times H^1$ with at most one derivative in either argument; formal symmetry and smooth density give $a(u,v)=\overline{a(v,u)}$. With real smooth cutoffs $\chi_i$ supported in charts and $\sum_i\chi_i^2=1$, positivity of $a^{ij}$ and of the bundle metric bounds $a(\chi_iu,\chi_iu)$ below by $c\|\partial(\chi_iu)\|_2^2$ minus lower terms; summing and absorbing gives $a(u,u)\ge c\|u\|_{H^1}^2-C\|u\|_2^2$, extended by density. For $\lambda>C+1$, $a_\lambda=a+\lambda(\cdot,\cdot)_2$ is coercive, so Lax-Milgram ([[thm-lax-milgram]]) gives a unique $Bf\in H^1$ with $a_\lambda(Bf,v)=(f,v)_2$ and a bound; the $H^2$ part gives $Bf\in H^2$ and $\|Bf\|_{H^2}\le C\|f\|_2$. The inverse identities $PB=I-\lambda B$ and $BP=I-\lambda B$ follow by testing; symmetry of $a_\lambda$ makes $B$ bounded selfadjoint; its range contains all smooth sections, hence is dense, and $Bf=0$ forces $f=0$. Compactness follows from the bounded $H^2$ range and $H^2\hookrightarrow L^2$ compact. Selfadjointness of the unbounded $P$ with domain exactly $H^2=\operatorname{ran}B$: for $A=P+\lambda$, $y\in\operatorname{dom}A^*$ gives $(f,y)_2=(Bf,A^*y)_2=(f,BA^*y)_2$ for all $f$, so $y=BA^*y\in H^2$ and $Ay=A^*y$; conversely symmetry puts $H^2\subseteq\operatorname{dom}A^*$. The $H^k\to H^{k+2}$ boundedness and smooth preservation of $B$ follow from the higher regularity estimate applied to $Pu=f-\lambda u$.

Parametrices (4): the inverse identities give $PB=I-\lambda B$ on $L^2$ and $BP=I-\lambda B$ on $H^2$; the error is compact on $L^2$ by the compactness of $B$, and on $H^2$ because $B:H^2\to H^4$ is bounded and $H^4\hookrightarrow H^2$ is compact. The Axiom of Choice supplies the countable-choice consequences used through the cited Rellich, Sobolev-embedding, partition and Lax-Milgram interfaces ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).
items.axiom_use: Full AC is assumed; it is used through the cited interfaces for smooth partitions of unity, Rellich compactness, higher-order Sobolev embedding and Lax-Milgram (countable choice), declared via def-axiom-of-choice and thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice. The statement is not choice-free.

items.title: Compact Laplace-type operators: smooth kernel, closed range and Green inverse
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M,E,P$ have exactly the compact, boundaryless, scalar-positive-symbol and formal symmetry hypotheses of [[thm-elliptic-differential-operators-on-compact-vector-bundles-have-parametrices-and-regularity]], with $\operatorname{dom}P=H^2(M,E)$. Write $\mathcal H=\ker P$.

Then $\mathcal H$ is finite dimensional and consists of smooth sections, $\operatorname{ran}P=\mathcal H^\perp$ is closed in $L^2$, and
$$L^2(M,E)=\mathcal H\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\operatorname{ran}P.$$
Let $\Pi$ be the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]). There is a unique linear operator $G:L^2\to H^2\cap\mathcal H^\perp$ with
$$PG=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad GP=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }H^2,\qquad G\Pi=\Pi G=0.$$
It is bounded from $H^k$ to $H^{k+2}$ for every integer $k\ge0$, compact and selfadjoint on $L^2$, and preserves smooth sections. For all such $k$,
$$H^k=\mathcal H\oplus P(H^{k+2}),\qquad C^\infty(M,E)=\mathcal H\oplus P(C^\infty(M,E)),$$
where the second summands are the corresponding intersections with $\mathcal H^\perp$, and the decompositions are topological. The projection is smoothing: for every integer $r\ge0$, $\|\Pi f\|_{C^r}\le C_r\|f\|_2$. Consequently $G$ is a two-sided parametrix with finite-rank smoothing remainders. If additionally $(Pu,u)_2\ge0$ for smooth $u$, then $P$ and $G$ are nonnegative on their respective domains.
items.strategy: Kernel: every $h\in\mathcal H$ lies in $H^2$, and the higher weak regularity of the preceding theorem at all orders makes $h$ smooth with $\|h\|_{H^2}\le C\|h\|_2$; the kernel is closed in $L^2$ because that estimate makes an $L^2$-convergent sequence Cauchy in $H^2$. If $\mathcal H$ were infinite dimensional, AC permits choosing successively an orthonormal sequence in it; the sequence is bounded in $H^2$, so $H^2\hookrightarrow L^2$ compactness gives an $L^2$-convergent subsequence, contradicting the distance $\sqrt2$ between distinct orthonormal vectors. Closed range and complement: there is $c>0$ with $\|u\|_2\le c\|Pu\|_2$ on $H^2\cap\mathcal H^\perp$; otherwise a sequence with $\|u_j\|_2=1$ and $\|Pu_j\|_2<1/j$ is bounded in $H^2$ by the elliptic estimate, a subsequence converges in $L^2$, the estimate applied to differences makes it Cauchy in $H^2$, and its limit would be a nonzero element of $\mathcal H\cap\mathcal H^\perp$, a contradiction. Combining with the elliptic estimate gives $\|u\|_{H^2}\le C'\|Pu\|_2$ on that complement, hence closed range: a convergent sequence $Pu_j$ can be corrected by the $\Pi$-projections (which do not change $Pu_j$), made Cauchy in $H^2$ and passed to the limit. A vector orthogonal to the range is exactly an element of $\operatorname{dom}P^*$ with $P^*y=0$, which by selfadjointness is $\mathcal H$; the closed-subspace orthogonal decomposition ([[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]]) gives $\operatorname{ran}P=\mathcal H^\perp$ and the $L^2$ splitting. Green operator: for $f\in\mathcal H^\perp$ choose a preimage in $H^2$ and subtract its harmonic projection; the result is the unique preimage in $H^2\cap\mathcal H^\perp$, and setting $Gf$ equal to it and $G=0$ on $\mathcal H$ gives linearity, the bounds and the two inverse identities; compactness follows from the $H^2$ bound and the compact inclusion, selfadjointness from symmetry of $P$ (harmonic cross terms vanish), and $G\Pi=\Pi G=0$ is immediate. Smoothing projection: a finite $L^2$-orthonormal basis $e_1,\dots,e_N$ of the finite-dimensional smooth space $\mathcal H$ gives $\Pi f=\sum_j(f,e_j)_2e_j$, so $\|\Pi f\|_{C^r}\le\sum_j\|f\|_2\|e_j\|_2\|e_j\|_{C^r}$. The $H^k\to H^{k+2}$ bounds follow from $PGf=f-\Pi f$ and the preceding regularity estimate, and give smooth preservation; the decompositions $H^k=\mathcal H\oplus P(H^{k+2})$ are then the inverse identities read at order $k$. Nonnegativity: if $(Pu,u)_2\ge0$ on smooth $u$, density and continuity extend it to $H^2$, and $(Gf,f)_2=(u,Pu)_2\ge0$ for $f\in\mathcal H^\perp$, $u=Gf$; finiteness and smoothing of the remainder give the parametrix statement.
items.axiom_use: Full AC as declared; used for the orthonormal-sequence choice in the finite-dimensionality argument and inherited through the orthogonal-decomposition and elliptic interfaces.

items.title: Harmonic representatives for compact de Rham and Dolbeault complexes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary, of real dimension at least two. Its metric defines the $L^2$ pairing on forms by the Riemannian density; orientation is unnecessary. Let $d^*$ denote the formal adjoint of $d$, and $\Delta=dd^*+d^*d$ on total real forms, or on their complexification. With domain $H^2$ the operator is nonnegative and selfadjoint. Its degreewise smooth kernels $\mathcal H^k$ are finite dimensional, and there is an orthogonal smooth decomposition
$$\Omega^k(M)=\mathcal H^k\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}d\Omega^{k-1}(M)\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}d^*\Omega^{k+1}(M).$$
The map $h\mapsto[h]$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal H^k\to H^k_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)$, over $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ as appropriate.

More generally let $X$ be a compact complex manifold of complex dimension $m\ge1$ with a smooth Hermitian metric. Let $E$ be a holomorphic bundle of finite rank with a smooth Hermitian metric. The holomorphic bundle structure supplies frames with holomorphic invertible transition matrices; the Hermitian metric is separate smooth positive-definite pairing data. On $E$-valued $(p,q)$ forms, define $\bar\partial_E$ by the coefficientwise Dolbeault operator in holomorphic bundle charts and let $\bar\partial_E^*$ be its formal adjoint. For each fixed $p$, $\Delta_{\bar\partial_E}=\bar\partial_E\bar\partial_E^*+\bar\partial_E^*\bar\partial_E$ on the sum over $q$ is nonnegative and selfadjoint on $H^2$; its smooth harmonic spaces $\mathcal H_E^{p,q}$ are finite dimensional and
$$\Omega^{p,q}(X,E)=\mathcal H_E^{p,q}\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\bar\partial_E\Omega^{p,q-1}(X,E)\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\bar\partial_E^*\Omega^{p,q+1}(X,E).$$
In particular harmonic forms represent the smooth Dolbeault quotient
$$H_{\bar\partial}^{p,q}(X,E):=\ker\bar\partial_E/\operatorname{im}\bar\partial_E$$
uniquely. Terms outside the degree range are zero. This asserts smooth Dolbeault cohomology; an identification with sheaf cohomology requires a separate Dolbeault-resolution comparison theorem.

For either complex write $D=d$ or $D=\bar\partial_E$, $P=DD^*+D^*D$, and let $\Pi,G$ be the preceding Green projection and inverse. They preserve degree, $G$ preserves smooth forms, and on smooth forms
$$DG=GD,\qquad D^*G=GD^*,\qquad D\Pi=\Pi D=D^*\Pi=\Pi D^*=0.$$
Every closed smooth $u$ satisfies $u=\Pi u+D(D^*Gu)$.
items.strategy: Formal adjoint: in a chart, integrate each coefficient derivative of $D$ once, transpose-conjugate its matrix and include the derivatives of the bundle metric and of the density; the local expressions have smooth coefficients of order at most one and satisfy the adjoint identity, and the partition-free construction and gluing of [[lem-formal-adjoints-of-differential-operators-exist-and-are-unique]] make them global. Uniqueness follows by testing the difference against all compactly supported smooth sections, so the local expressions agree on overlaps. Hence $D^*$ exists as a smooth differential operator, $P=DD^*+D^*D$ is formally symmetric with $(Pu,u)_2=\|Du\|_2^2+\|D^*u\|_2^2\ge0$, and it is Laplace type: for $d$, the positive-frequency principal symbol is $i\varepsilon(\xi)$, that of $d^*$ is $-i\iota(\xi^\sharp)$, and the contraction product rule $\iota(\xi^\sharp)(\xi\wedge v)=|\xi|^2v-\xi\wedge\iota(\xi^\sharp)v$, checked on wedge monomials by deleting each factor with its alternating sign, gives $\varepsilon(\xi)\iota(\xi^\sharp)+\iota(\xi^\sharp)\varepsilon(\xi)=|\xi|^2I$, hence $\sigma_2(P)=|\xi|^2I$. For $\bar\partial_E$, in a holomorphic frame the coefficients transform by holomorphic matrices ([[def-e-valued-dolbeault-operators-and-ltwo-structure]]), and the same unitary wedge-basis identity gives $\sigma_2(P)=\frac12|\xi|^2I$ (equivalently $|\xi^{0,1}|^2I$), a smooth positive-definite scalar quadratic form; the general theory of [[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]] applies with the bundle $\Lambda^kT^*M$ or $\Lambda^{p,q}T^*X\otimes E$. Applying [[thm-sobolev-compactness-and-elliptic-estimates-give-fredholm-hodge-decomposition]] to $P$ gives a finite-dimensional smooth kernel $\mathcal H$, closed range $\mathcal H^\perp$ and the Green pair $\Pi,G$ with $PG=GP=I-\Pi$; smoothness of harmonic elements and the $H^k$-bounds hold in every degree, and degree preservation follows because $D$ and $D^*$ change degree by $\pm1$ and $P$ preserves it. Commutation: for smooth $u$, $P(DGu)=D(PGu)=D(u-\Pi u)=Du$; both $DGu$ and $Du$ are orthogonal to $\mathcal H$, so uniqueness of the orthogonal solution gives $DG=GD$, and the same argument gives $D^*G=GD^*$; orthogonality of the images gives $D\Pi=\Pi D=D^*\Pi=\Pi D^*=0$. Decomposition and representatives: the Green identity $u=\Pi u+DD^*Gu+D^*DGu$ is an orthogonal sum (the harmonic term is orthogonal to both images, and $(Da,D^*b)_2=(D^2a,b)_2=0$), and conversely every harmonic or image form lies in the displayed ambient space; so $\Omega^k=\mathcal H^k\oplus d\Omega^{k-1}\oplus d^*\Omega^{k+1}$, with the analogous bidegree statement for $\bar\partial_E$. If $Du=0$, then $DGu=GDu=0$, so $u=\Pi u+D(D^*Gu)$; harmonic forms are closed, giving surjectivity of $h\mapsto[h]$ onto the smooth closed/exact quotient, while a harmonic exact form $h=Dv$ has $\|h\|_2^2=(Dv,h)_2=(v,D^*h)_2=0$, giving injectivity and uniqueness. Finite dimensionality is that of $\mathcal H$. Endpoint degrees are handled by interpreting the out-of-range operators as zero. The trivial line bundle on the de Rham side and the case $p=q=0$ on the Dolbeault side are included; no sheaf comparison is used or asserted ([[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]], [[thm-d-dbar-decomposition-and-identities]]).

items.title: Flat torus harmonic forms are constant-coefficient forms
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, $n\ge2$ and an integer $k\ge0$, with $\binom nk=0$ when $k>n$. On $T^n=\mathbb R^n/\mathbb Z^n$ with its flat metric, the forms $dx^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{i_k}$, $i_1<\cdots<i_k$, form a basis of $\mathcal H^k$. Every real de Rham class therefore has a unique constant-coefficient representative, and $\dim H^k_{\mathrm{dR}}(T^n)=\binom nk$.
items.strategy: Verification 1.1 proves compactness from the unit cube and coframe descent from translational quotient charts. Verification 2.1 uses repeated Riemann integration and Newton–Leibniz to prove periodic integration by parts, d*=−sum iota_j partial_j, the coefficientwise Laplacian and energy. Verification 3.1 proves harmonic iff constant coefficient, counts increasing wedge monomials and uses the Hodge representative isomorphism, including k=0,n and k>n.
items.axiom_use: Full AC inherited from the Hodge theorem [[thm-hodge-laplacian-kernel-represents-de-rham-and-dolbeault-cohomology]]; the flat-torus geometry uses only countable choice.
